items.page_hint: Ch 16, §3 and Fig 16.1 caption

The arithmetic in the chapter uses $0.0208 per request, which is $20.80 per 1,000 requests.

items.evidence: Quote found (normalized) at chapter-16.md L236 'the ~7.5 M canonical-price point at \$20.80 per 1M tokens (≈\$0.0208 per 1K-token request)' and in the Fig 16.1 caption L264 '\$20.80 per 1M tokens (≈\$0.0208 per 1K-token request) API'. At the labeled token price a 9,500-token request costs 20.80 × 9,500/1e6 = $0.1976 (finding's figure recomputed), and the break-even divisions use it per request (L190 '$155,816.93 ÷ $0.0208', L192 '$155,816.93 ÷ $0.0208 = 7,491,198.56'). items.page_hint: Ch 16 §3 ('Reading the result'; 'Parametric sensitivity is the durable form'; 'When each wins'); Note 16.1-1; Fig 16.1 caption
items.issue: The API price is $0.002/1K input and $0.008/1K output, i.e. $2.00 and $8.00 per 1M tokens. At the canonical 9,200/300 mix the blended rate is $0.0208 per request = $2.19 per 1M tokens, not $20.80. '$20.80 per 1M tokens' overstates the token price by ~9.5x, and '$0.0208 per 1K-token request' misplaces the denominator by 1000x (it is per request). Worse, the shorthand '$20.8/1K' is used in the same chapter for the API's cost per 1,000 requests ($129,792 / 6.24M x 1000 = $20.8), so one token carries two incompatible meanings; a reader who reads '$20.8/1K' as $/1K-requests computes a break-even 1000x too small.

items.fix_instruction: State the API price once as '$0.0208 per request at the canonical mix (= $2.19 per 1M blended tokens; $2.00/1M input, $8.00/1M output)'. Replace every '$X/1K' price label (L126, L161, L190, L236, L264) with '$X per 1M tokens' or '$0.0XX per request'; reserve '$/1K req' for cost per 1,000 requests.

items.page_hint: Ch 16 §8 mini-case, opening paragraph
items.issue: Four 2-GPU replicas on one 8-GPU host require 4 x 140 GB = 560 GB of the 640 GB pool for weights alone, leaving ~80 GB before the ~64 GB runtime reserve — about 16 GB of KV per host, i.e. 0.6 of a 9,500-token request. The mini-case's own geometry therefore cannot hold the full-context KV the book's arithmetic requires, and the 'well inside' capacity claim is unsupported. The comparator is also undisclosed: 0.48 equals 40 / 84, i.e. it silently treats the canonical 21-host fleet as 84 two-GPU replicas, whereas the canonical fleet is 21 eight-GPU hosts (1.905 rps/replica).

items.fix_instruction: State the mini-case's replica geometry explicitly and price its memory (4 × 140 GB = 560 GB of the 640 GB pool, 16 GB KV left = 0.64 requests), show the in-flight population (2 rps × 8.6 s = 17) against that budget, and derive the 0.48 rps/replica comparator from the canonical fleet's replica count with the derivation printed.

items.page_hint: Ch 16 §8 mini-case, verdict paragraph
items.issue: The analysis concludes self-hosting is ~$64K/mo cheaper unless the opportunity cost of the engineer's time exceeds ~$90K/mo — a quantity the mini-case never measures. The verdict nonetheless selects the API, which is only correct if that unmeasured opportunity cost is above $90K/mo. The verdict therefore asserts a conclusion the reasoning does not support, and it contradicts the chapter's own closing sentence ('A team that cannot say that, or that has a second engineer to spare, runs the same numbers and buys the servers').

items.issue: Table 12-1 records a passing checkmark for the TTFT SLO and §3 asserts the latency budget is met, while Table 12-2 in the same chapter records the SLO as unmeasured and the verdict as 'conditional'. The chapter's own gate discipline (a candidate that fails a gate is eliminated; a gate that is open is not a pass) is violated by the checkmark.
items.quoted_clause: Table 12-1: '✓ memory 164 < 640 GB · ✓ TTFT SLO (median ≤1.2 s, p95 ≤2 s)' | §3: 'per-request prefill + decode stay within the latency budget thanks to prefix caching and the high bandwidth of 8×H100' | Table 12-2: '**? unmeasured** — peak prefill and SLO not demonstrated; illustrative screen only'
items.fix_instruction: Replace the ✓ in the SLO column of Table 12-1 with the '? unmeasured' status used in Table 12-2 (or '✓ (design target, unmeasured)'), and rewrite §3 to 'per‑request prefill + decode are expected to stay within the latency budget at the admitted load; this is the SLO gate that Ch 14 must close'. Keep ✓ for memory (a deterministic calculation).
items.evidence: All three parts verified by grep in chapter-12.md: Table 12-1: '✓ memory 164 < 640 GB · ✓ TTFT SLO (median ≤1.2 s, p95 ≤2 s) | **conditional finalist**'; §3: 'Throughput at the SLO: per‑request prefill + decode stay within the latency budget thanks to prefix caching and the high bandwidth of 8×H100, but the sustained rate fails at one host...'; Table 12-2: '| Feasibility at declared SLO | **? unmeasured** — peak prefill and SLO not demonstrated; illustrative screen only |...'. The same chapter records the same TTFT SLO gate as ✓ passed in one table and ? unmeasured in another — a contradiction with the gate discipline ('a gate that is open is not a pass').

items.issue: Two coupled problems in the verdict boxes. (1) Vocabulary: 'CLEARS CAPACITY GATE (a)(b)' uses a gate name that appears nowhere in the caption's gate set (MEM/THR/QUAL), so the reader cannot tell which gate was cleared. (2) Verdict strength vs load point: the green OUTCOME vs red hatched GATED layout reads as a settled pass/fail, while the caption states all three candidates have 'its own open validation gate (not a settled verdict)' and printed 211 states the candidate 'is not a validated survivor'; and the supporting number 'each needs ~5 hosts of prefill capacity' is the average-load (92K tok/s) figure, whereas Table 12-2 gives peak ~19 hosts and 'Peak headroom (N-1): not demonstrated' for both (a) and (b). The figure therefore omits a 4x peak and an undemonstrated headroom while appearing to certify capacity.
items.fix_instruction: In Fig 12.1's OUTCOME box use a caption gate name (THR/throughput) instead of 'CAPACITY GATE' and label the load point: '~5 prefill hosts at 10 rps avg / ~19 at 40 rps peak, N−1 headroom not demonstrated (Table 12-2)'.
items.evidence: p233 figure reads 'CLEARS CAPACITY GATE (a) · (b) / each needs ~5 hosts of prefill capacity' while caption (chapter-12.md:103) defines only MEM/THR/QUAL gates; p231 Table 12-2 rows (chapter-12.md:113-114) give avg '~5' vs peak '~19 ... before headroom' and 'Peak headroom (N−1): not demonstrated' for (a),(b) — the figure certifies capacity using only the average-load number.

items.issue: The ④ OUTCOME box asserts 'CLEARS CAPACITY GATE (a)·(b)' with the sub-line 'each needs ~5 hosts of prefill capacity', but ~5 hosts is the AVERAGE-load figure (10 rps × 9.2K-in = 92K tok/s ÷ 19.8K). The ② CONSTRAINTS box in the same figure lists '10/40 rps', and Table 12-2 (p.211) shows the PEAK requirement is ~19 hosts for (a) and marks 'Peak headroom (N−1): not demonstrated' for (a) and (b). So the figure's positive verdict is only valid at average load and directly contradicts the table's 'not demonstrated' headroom row; a reader infers 5 hosts satisfy the SLO, which is false at peak.
